title: Why Won’t My Dryer Start?

seo.title: Why Won’t My Dryer Start?
seo.meta_description: If your dryer will not start, check power, the door, control settings, and signs of electrical trouble before assuming an internal part failed.
seo.search_intent: Diagnose a dryer that will not start by separating power and control issues from internal faults that need service.

excerpt: A dryer that does nothing may have a simple power or control problem, or it may have stopped because an internal safety device or component failed. Start with checks that do not require opening the cabinet.
content_html:
If you press Start and nothing happens, first separate “no power” from “has power but will not run.” That one observation narrows the problem quickly.

See whether the control panel is alive

If the display and lights are dead, check the plug and electrical panel. Full-size electric dryers often use a high-voltage double-pole circuit. Reset a tripped breaker once; if it trips again, stop rather than repeatedly resetting it.

If the panel works, check the door and controls

The door must close far enough to operate its safety switch. Remove clothing caught in the opening and make sure the latch engages. Also look for Control Lock, Child Lock, Delay Start, or another setting that can prevent an immediate start.

Some dryers require a deliberate Start press

On certain models you must hold Start for a second or two rather than tap it. Follow the panel or manual. If the dryer hums but the drum does not begin moving, you have moved beyond a simple setting issue.

Do not bypass a safety switch

A door switch, thermal fuse, motor, belt switch, or control can prevent operation. Diagnosing those parts requires cabinet access and electrical testing; gas dryers add fuel-system hazards. Do not defeat an interlock just to see whether the machine will run.

Stop using it when the symptoms are electrical

Unplug the dryer and arrange service if you smell burning insulation, see heat damage at the receptacle, hear electrical arcing, find a damaged cord, or the breaker trips again. If the controls look normal but the machine simply will not start, tell the technician exactly what the panel does and whether you hear a click or hum.

A useful order is power, door, controls, then motor response. Once those external checks are exhausted, internal diagnosis is the next level.

faq.question: Should I keep resetting the breaker?
faq.answer: No. Reset it once. If it trips again, leave the dryer off and have the circuit or appliance checked.

faq.question: Can a bad door latch stop the dryer?
faq.answer: Yes. The dryer may refuse to run if the door does not operate its safety switch.

faq.question: Should I open the dryer to test the thermal fuse?
faq.answer: Not as a basic homeowner check. Internal testing involves electrical components and should be done only with appropriate service procedures.
